claim.summary: Over a commutative coefficient ring, let C be a degree-D pseudoideal and w_1..w_r polynomials. If s has degree <=sigma, s w_i - w_i lies in C for every i and s p lies in C, then f=1-s kills every w_i and f p - p lies in C, so f preserves p modulo C; a sufficient case is s = sum_i a_i w_i with w_i p in C and deg a_i + deg w_i + deg p <= D, and then s^2 = s modulo C when deg a_i + sigma + deg w_i <= D. Over a field, if C is the degree-D part of the vanishing ideal of a finite X and k <= min(D - max deg w_i, D - deg p), a polynomial f of degree <=k kills every w_i with fp outside C exactly when f vanishes on the union Z of the w_i's supports on X and not at every point of supp(p) minus Z; the first such degree is an interpolation degree on X. On the cube 1-s is the reduced product of denominators; for pigeonhole hole factors it is the empty-column indicator.

claim.summary: For finitely many module errors vanishing after localization and a protected element surviving there, a product of denominators kills all errors and preserves the element, with additive filtration cost. Fixed linear common-kernel survival descends across finite field extensions without degree increase. Controls: in k[x,y]/(x,y)^2 no annihilator of (x) preserves y; in k[t]/t^(m+1) annihilators of (t) first occur at degree m; in k[u,v]/(u^2,v^2) useful f=u is nilpotent and localization at it is zero; rank-one error data at t distinct evaluation points still require locator degree at least t.
claim.assessment: Working elementary transfer proofs and exact algebraic counterexamples, passed by the sole medium reviewer. Finite-extension scope retained for the motivating use. Support, matrix rank and scalar extension alone give no universal cheap multiplier theorem.

claim.summary: Over any field, let C be a degree-D PC closure, w_1..w_r of degrees e_i<=e, Ann_K(w)={u in V_K: wu in C}, and s=sum_i a_i w_i with deg a_i+e_i<=K', deg s<=sigma, s w_i - w_i in C for every i, K+K'<=D and K+sigma+e<=D. Then intersection_i Ann_K(w_i)=Ann_K(s): the common kernel of the factor maps is one annihilator. Errors E_nu=h_nu w_{i(nu)}+(member) with deg h_nu<=g and K+e+g<=D have that common kernel inside theirs. In a domain model on a finite X with 0/1-valued w_i, s=1-prod(1-w_i) qualifies when K+(r+1)e<=D; for the pigeonhole hole axioms, w_i=x_ij (i in I) and s=sum_{i in I} x_ij qualify when K+2<=D.

claim.summary: Over any field F, for a finite set X in F^n, B_D the polynomials of degree <=D vanishing on X, U=V_K/(B_D cap V_K) and errors E_1..E_s of degree <=e with K+e<=D: the map u->[E_j u] in V_D/B_D has rank dim U|_{S_j}, S_j the support of E_j on X, and the stacked map has rank dim U|_S, S the union of the supports; the restriction U|_S -> direct sum of U|_{S_j} is injective, so the sum of ranks exceeds the stacked rank by its cokernel dimension. With X the Boolean cube over F_p this is the domain-only model of cor:pang-observation-calibration at Pang's cutoff Delta+K+d<=D, where every saving over the sum is a union-of-supports interpolation count; such savings carry into Pang's proper quotient since B_D is inside C_D.

claim.summary: Over any field (multilinear ring, or Boolean axioms among G), let G and P be finite sets of polynomials, H the degree-D PC closure of G, P_D the members of P of degree exactly D, and every member of P of degree >= D. The degree-D closure of G with P equals H + span P_D, with the same members of degree below D as H, if and only if (H + span P_D) cap V_{D-1} lies in H; it suffices that the degree-D parts of P_D are linearly independent modulo the degree-D parts of members of H. For the product pigeonhole system over any field (pigeon axioms prod_j(1-x_ij) of degree n, hole axioms) and D <= n, H is the degree-D part of the vanishing ideal of the hole-respecting assignments and the closure's members of degree below D are those of H.
